subject: Provisional GPU bucket request + roadmap impact (Q4 UX eval)
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Provisional GPU bucket request + roadmap impact (Q4 UX eval)

Team —

Quick ask: product is kicking off a short UX evaluation next month that needs a provisional dedicated GPU bucket for a model-sensitivity sweep. This is a 3-week pilot starting 2026-11-01 with two tight sweep windows where we may burst beyond standard autoscale limits for up to 48 hours total.

What we need:
- Provisional reservation: 12 x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved for the pilot baseline (dedicated pool).
- Autoscale exception: ability to temporarily burst to 30 GPUs for 24-48 hour windows (max 48 hours cumulative across the pilot) without being evicted by normal preemption.
- Lead time: need confirmation by 2026-10-18 to lock infra changes and update the roadmaps.

Why this matters: the sweep will feed quantitative UX metrics for the feature decision (latency vs quality trade-offs). If we can lock a small dedicated bucket + controlled burst, product can complete the evaluation without noise from noisy multi-tenant queues. Marissa, this directly affects the Q4 milestone you flagged last week.

Attached: capacity_snapshot_q4-ux-eval.csv (current pool usage) and provisional_mou_draft.pdf (template MOU I put together for temporary carve-outs).

Questions for infra (David/Marcus):
1) Is a 12->30 burst feasible without changing allocator code or just a reservations/ops policy exception?
2) What is the rollback / fallback if cluster pressure spikes? (e.g., preemptible fallback, throttling)
3) Rough ops cost estimate for 2x 24-hour bursts.

If we can get yes/no + a short plan by EOD Friday (2026-10-18) I can coordinate with product and legal to finalize the MOU.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11T10:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Provisional GPU bucket request + roadmap impact (Q4 UX eval)

Kimberly — thanks for the heads up. A few clarifying points before I commit ops time: 

- Isolation: do you need full tenant isolation (no noisy neighbor throttling) or just guaranteed capacity for the listed VMs? Full isolation implies carving from a dedicated physical pool or reserved slice, which is heavier on infra.
- Burst mechanics: are we expecting a single contiguous 48-hour burst or multiple shorter bursts? You mentioned "two tight sweep windows" — need exact schedule windows (approx dates/times) to verify cluster calendar conflicts.
- Priority: where should this rank relative to known major commitments in Nov (IRIS training sweep on Nov 10-14 and marketplace rollout Nov 22)? If higher priority, we need leadership sign-off to change preemption policy during those dates.

Operational impact & quick estimate: 12 -> 30 A100-eq for 48 hours is feasible as an ops policy exception if we can accept preemption fallback during system-wide pressure. If you require non-preemptible, we need to carve physical capacity which will increase cost and requires procurement lead time (~2 weeks). I'll sketch a cost delta and a short ops runbook (attached: ops_capacity_note.md).

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Kimberly: confirm isolation requirement and provide the two target windows.
- Marcus: can you comment on allocator/ops changes (I think this can be policy + reservations in the short term).

-David

--
David Kim
Head of Infra & Capacity
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T07:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Provisional GPU bucket request + roadmap impact (Q4 UX eval)

Quick note from allocation side:

- Short answer: doable as a policy-level carve (reserved bucket + temporary autoscale top-up), no allocator code changes required for a one-off pilot. We already support temporary reservations and burst policies for pilots; this can reuse that path.
- Fallbacks: recommend we implement a preemptible-tier fallback: baseline 12 non-preemptible, burst GPUs as preemptible with a clear eviction policy. That keeps cost down and avoids wholesale pool carving.
- Scheduling: we need the exact UTC windows to check against other scheduled maintenance and IRIS sweep. If any conflicts with IRIS high-priority, we should consider shifting pilot by 72 hours.
- Approval: ops policy exceptions for burst caps >25 GPUs require sign-off from Product Ops (Kimberly) and Infra (David) and an entry in the capacity runbook. Leadership only if we want non-preemptible guaranteed burst.

I'll reserve tentative ops time next week to prepare the runbook and a short rollback playbook. Laura — can you confirm the UX evaluation's hard cutoff date so we can align?

Marcus
Sr. Capacity Planner, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Provisional GPU bucket request + roadmap impact (Q4 UX eval)

Thanks, all. Context and clarifications from Product: 
- We can schedule the two sweep windows: Nov 4-5 (UTC) and Nov 16-17 (UTC). Each window is expected to consume ~20-30 GPUs for ~12-18 hours each. Cumulative burst demand should not exceed 48 hours.
- Isolation: we do not require full physical isolation. We want predictable performance for the baseline tests — baseline 12 non-preemptible GPUs + burst into preemptible slots is fine by us as long as we get a consistent QoS for baseline runs.
- Trade-offs: if ops prefers a step approach, Product is willing to start with 12 baseline + ability to step to 18 for the first sweep and 30 for the second sweep if signals look good. This staged approach reduces risk and cost.
- Metrics Product will report back: mean latency (95/99), quality delta vs current model, and token cost per inference.

I'll sign the provisional_mou_draft once we lock the windows and fallback. Happy to join the runbook sync.

-Marissa
PM, Model UX
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T14:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Provisional GPU bucket request + roadmap impact (Q4 UX eval)

All — thanks for the fast turnaround. Summary and next steps: 
1) Confirmed windows: Nov 4-5 and Nov 16-17 UTC. Product accepts baseline 12 non-preemptible + burst into preemptible up to 30, with staged step option (12->18->30) if ops recommends that cadence.
2) David/Marcus: please prepare a short ops runbook with fallback (preemption thresholds, throttle rules) and a cost delta by EOD 2026-10-18. Attach to the MOU and post to the runbook folder.
3) Marissa: please sign the provisional_mou_draft and add the metric checklist.
4) I'll set up a 30-minute sync on 2026-10-15 10:00am PT to finalize runbook and sign-off (invite to follow).

Action items assigned. If anything changes on scheduling I will update immediately.

Thanks —
Kimberly
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
